_README: Error rates for the rules that decide what the Index publishes. Each was measured against a hand-judged sample drawn by seeded shuffle; `npm run validate -- --full` redraws the same samples. Intervals are Wilson 95%.

overExclusion.how: full census of every withdrawn domain; homepage fetched, title and description read by hand
overExclusion.note: This is the classifier's own rate, which is what it should be: all 4 are corrected in classification-overrides.json, so the shipped pipeline removes none of them today. Checking this turned up that 2 of the 4 — dragonball-super.com and strikerreport.com — had their verdict fixed but were never put back in the audit list, so their report pages were live while they stayed out of the ranking and out of every weekly run. Both are now in submitted.txt and rejoin at the next run.

asShipped.note: after overrides. The 4 raw errors are the measure of the model, not of what the site publishes.

underExclusion.pool: e15d222a8342 — 1,175 kept domains, the panel as published. Every figure below is measured on this one pool.
underExclusion.how: Three draws of 66 on the same pool — `npm run probe-filter` with SEED=2026, 1337 and 5150 — 189 distinct domains, 9 drawn by more than one seed, 174 judged. The rule for 'unreadable' prints at the top of every run, so it travels with the output rather than being cited to a line number.
underExclusion.tiers: 148 judged on the page itself, 26 on robots/sitemap paths only, 15 on nothing.
underExclusion.sampling: Pseudo-random with a fixed seed over the whole kept pool. The pool is sorted first to canonicalise the order the shuffle acts on; sorting fixes the order, it does not select, and every member of the pool can be drawn.

wholePopulationBound.how: the far edge: all 15 domains that stayed unreadable plus all 26 judged only from robots.txt and sitemap.xml, counted as wrong keeps. URL paths say what a site is made of but are not the page, so a bound leaning on them is not the far edge.
wholePopulationBound.says: at the far edge of the interval, at most 28.1% of kept domains are wrongly kept. Nothing weaker covers the whole sample.
wholePopulationBound.intermediate: Counting only the unresolved as wrong and trusting the robots/sitemap tier: 15/189 = 7.9%, 95% CI 4.9-12.7%.

underExclusion.zeroMeansWhat: Zero errors on this pool is not evidence that the filter is clean. The one error it is known to make — az24.vn, a Vietnamese lottery-results site — was found by a draw on the previous pool and then excluded, which is what changed the pool. Read this as: after that fix, three fresh draws found nothing more, and the upper bound on what they could have missed is 2.2% among domains that could be read and 28.1% across the whole sample.

priorPool.result: two draws, 127 distinct domains, 111 judged, 1 wrong keep (az24.vn) = 0.9%, 95% CI 0.2-4.9%
priorPool.why_separate: kept apart rather than pooled with the three draws above, because a rate pooled across two different populations describes neither.

underExclusion.handJudged: 20 flags across the three draws, none upheld. Rejected with their evidence: player slots (aternos.org), PCIe slots (asus.com), a calendar slot (tawk.to), a waiver slot in practice software (therapservices.net), CSS size tokens xxx-large (ew.com, allrecipes.com), a Tailwind attribute data-[slot=icon] (vercel.com), a masked IP 141.171.31.XXX (powerbi.com), a JSON-LD placeholder "XXX" (xe.com), OnlyFans headlines (index.hr, infobae.com), betting-prosecution stories (cricbuzz.com, news18.com), Las Vegas hotel listings (priceline.com), and a bingo link in a tabloid's games nav (mirror.co.uk).
underExclusion.sensitivity: Two judgement calls were kept and are published rather than buried. goal.com age-gates gambling advertising ("This site contains gambling advertising for 24+") and livescore.com sells betting-affiliate placement; both are kept because the rule judges primary purpose and both are sports news. Counted as errors instead, the rate is 2/174 = 1.1%, 95% CI 0.3-4.1%, and the far edge is unchanged.
underExclusion.reproducibility: The earlier 0/121 was drawn from the leaderboard in score order, so each weekly run reshuffled the pool and the same seed drew a different sample — reproducible in name only, failing silently. The pool is now sorted and fingerprinted, the fingerprint prints on every run and is recorded here, and POOL_HASH=<hash> turns a changed pool into a loud mismatch instead of a quietly different measurement.
underExclusion.supersedes: 0/44 readable CI 0-8.0%; the single-seed 0/61; 0/121 CI 0-3.1%; and the 1/156 pooled across two pools, which described neither of them.

inSample.how: seed 42, 15 sites x 4 categories — the set the rule was tuned against, so not evidence of accuracy

heldOut.how: seed 99, disjoint from seed 42, 10 readable sites x 4 categories
heldOut.note: SUPERSEDED as the current rate by heldOutPostFix. Retained because it is what the rule scored before clarin.com and grow.google were fixed.

heldOutPostFix.how: seed 777, disjoint from seeds 42 and 99; 14 readable sites x 4 categories, judged by hand
heldOutPostFix.note: measured after the clarin.com and grow.google fixes. Pre-fix on seed 99 the held-out rate was 10%.
heldOutPostFix.checked: mega.nz 0/20 and bankofamerica.com 5/20 looked like under-credits and were verified correct: mega.nz serves a one-word JS shell, bankofamerica.com links no privacy page from its homepage HTML.

falsePositive.note: three detections is too few to support a rate; each was hand-checked against platform runtime config, not the detector's own patterns

shopMembership.how: seed 11, 20 domains marked shop, judged by hand
shopMembership.boundary: A shop is a site whose primary purpose is selling goods or services to the public and where a visitor can start a purchase. News, reference, social, government, sport, banking and free tools are not shops even when they sell a subscription. Whether to narrow this to retail only is a product decision, not a measurement one.
